title: Preserve queued request capacity when replacing retired middleware
goal: Replace ConcurrencyLimiter middleware with a global concurrency rate limiter while preserving capacity, queue order and rejection behavior under saturation.

runtime.name: .NET
runtime.reason: ASP.NET Core 11 supplies the new surface; exact observed runtime is RC2, not GA evidence.

sdk.name: .NET SDK
sdk.reason: Build the net11.0 application with an SDK supporting that target; sample pin is 11.0.100-rc.2.26504.105.

language.name: C#
language.reason: Declared canonical sample mode; older comparison uses C# 14 with SDK 10.0.402.

packageAssets: Microsoft.AspNetCore.App net11.0 shared framework and Microsoft.NETCore.App runtime assets. The comparison uses corresponding net10.0 assets. No separate package for the new API.
providers: Kestrel loopback HTTP server; process-local state only. No account, database or remote service.
platforms: ASP.NET Core supported server platforms; actually executed on Windows x64 only. No browser/WASI, native, AOT or cross-platform execution claim.
renderingModes: Server HTTP endpoints; no Blazor rendering mode.
prerequisites: Save each complete sample in its own directory with the shown SDK/project/build/package files. Restore framework packs before executing. The installed guidance is offline.
constraints: The retired middleware source has been removed and no new Microsoft.AspNetCore.ConcurrencyLimiter 11.x package ships. An older package may be retained temporarily; this recipe verifies it only on net10.0, not a net11.0 retained-package route. The replacement is shared-framework middleware with one global partition, PermitLimit=1, QueueLimit=1, OldestFirst and explicit 503 rejection to preserve the historical behavior. A concurrency limiter bounds simultaneous executions, not requests per time interval. Limits are per process, not distributed; no Retry-After estimate is available from concurrency alone.
stabilityLimitations: Stable API intent prepared from pinned .NET 11 RC2 artifacts under ADR 0004; GA reconciliation remains pending. No experimental opt-in applies.

evidence.scope: Actual Windows x64 .NET 10.0.13 compilation/execution with Microsoft.AspNetCore.ConcurrencyLimiter 10.0.13 net10.0 asset: 4 concurrent/sequential loopback requests; one executing, one queued, one 503 rejection; queued request completes after release; fourth request recovers; maximum active=1. Local CS0618 suppression only for historical use.

Actual Windows x64 .NET 11 RC2 compilation/execution with no added package: same 4 real HTTP requests through a single global concurrency partition, one queued, one explicit 503 rejection, queued admission after release and permit recovery; maximum active=1. No mocks, cross-compilation or distributed quota claim.

humanProof.scope: Focused HTTP behavior runs locally without owner-only resources. Does not settle product-wide client/platform coverage or GA/publication gates.
